Our class went to a small park for an outdoor activity. We were not racing. Our teacher, Ms Hall, wanted us to practise noticing things and following instructions. Each group would walk with an adult helper.

At the gate, she showed us a compass. Its red needle pointed north. She turned the compass, then asked us to watch what the needle did. We took turns holding it flat.

![词义图示：a compass](build/english-benchmark-authority-20261017/grade7-gloss-compass-v0.1.svg)

She also carried a whistle. Two short blows meant that everyone should stop and listen. She demonstrated the sound while we were all together. It was a signal, not the start of a (1) ____.

![词义图示：a whistle](build/english-benchmark-authority-20261017/grade7-gloss-whistle-v0.1.svg)

Our helper took us to a tree with a yellow ribbon. Beside it stood a little blue flag with a card attached. "Look under the empty bench," the card said. Max ran towards the nearest bench, but our helper reminded him that we should stay (2) ____ as a group.

There were two benches. One had a family sitting on it. We looked under the (3) ____ one and found a red envelope. Inside was a photograph of the park gate. We recognised the clock above it. That was where we should return.

On the way back, we saw another blue flag. Max thought we had to collect it. I reread our card. It said to follow the messages, not take the flags. We left it (4) ____ it was, so the next group could use it.

At the gate, Ms Hall blew two short notes. Everyone stopped. She asked us to describe one thing we had learned. Max said he had learned not to run ahead. I said a familiar colour did not mean every flag belonged to our group; we still needed to (5) ____ the instructions.

Ms Hall smiled. We had returned with only an envelope, but we had done everything on our list. There was no prize for arriving first. Our success came from working as a (6) ____, not from being faster than another group.
